title: Route-level A/B testing — Beta partner tracker (Console-first)
content:
Last updated: 2026-03-06 (Simran)

Purpose
- Single place to track who is in the route-level A/B testing beta, what they’re testing, expected success metrics, and issues/risk.
- This is the “source of truth” for weekly readiness + Support/CS handoffs.

Definitions (for consistency)
- Route under test: a single gateway route + project (e.g., /v1/chat/completions for project prj_…)
- Experiment ID: Redwood control-plane experiment ID (shown in Console + used for dashboards)
- Split: % traffic allocated per variant (deterministic assignment; see ADR-0187)
- Guardrails: auto-rollback thresholds (see SRE requirements email + guardrail policy doc)
- Hash key semantics: what we’re using for stickiness. Default target is api_key_id + (optional) x-redwood-user-id header if customer provides it.

Operational notes
- Before enabling: confirm feature flag AB_TESTING_BETA enabled for tenant + project; confirm exposure events visible; confirm dashboards populate within ~10–15 minutes.
- If partner is Dedicated: confirm pool capacity headroom before raising split >20%.
- If partner sees variant flipping: check whether they’re missing stickiness headers or using multiple API keys behind a load balancer.

============================================================
TAB: Enablement checklist (internal)
============================================================
- [ ] Entitlement: AB_TESTING_BETA enabled for tenant + project
- [ ] Route identified (no overlap with active canary on same route)
- [ ] Hash key + stickiness requirements communicated to customer
- [ ] Exposure logs visible in telemetry (verify within 15m)
- [ ] Results dashboard populating (latency/cost/errors per variant)
- [ ] Guardrails configured (thresholds agreed) + auto-rollback ON
- [ ] Runbook linked for Support + SRE oncall
- [ ] If eval suite attached: suite run schedule + minimum sample sizes shared
